blocks.text:
GET    /v1/users/42/orders?status=paid&limit=20&cursor=eyJpZCI6...   # list, filtered, paginated
POST   /v1/orders                     Idempotency-Key: 7f3c…        # create
GET    /v1/orders/981                                              # read
PATCH  /v1/orders/981   If-Match: "v7"  {"shipping_address": …}     # partial update, optimistic lock
DELETE /v1/orders/981

items: Nouns for resources, HTTP verbs for actions; plural collections.
**Cursor pagination** (opaque cursor encoding the last key) instead of offset for large or changing lists.
Idempotency keys on POSTs that create side effects; ETag/If-Match for concurrent edits.
Version in the path (/v1) or header; never break existing clients.
Consistent errors: status code + machine-readable code + message.

blocks.caption: Gateway tier holds connections; pub/sub routes messages
Delivering a message to a user connected to another gateway

items: Gateways are thin: auth, heartbeats, and relaying; business logic stays in stateless services.
On deploy or crash, clients reconnect (with jittered backoff) and resume from a last-seen sequence number.
Heartbeats (ping/pong every ~30 s) detect dead connections behind NATs and proxies.
Sign payloads (HMAC with a per-endpoint secret) and include a timestamp to prevent replay.
Deliver at-least-once from an outbox with exponential backoff over hours/days; expose a delivery log and manual redelivery.
Receivers dedupe on event id and respond 2xx fast, processing asynchronously.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Public CRUD is REST with cursor pagination and idempotency keys; internal calls are gRPC; live updates use WebSockets through a gateway tier with a connection registry and pub/sub, falling back to SSE where only server-to-client is needed.
